sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the third respondent/insurer in O.P.(MV) No.935/2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Pathanamthitta (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the Award dated 15/11/2019.
The respondent herein is the claim petitioner in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 28/04/2015 at about 08:15 a.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-23/K/5101 through Kottayam-Kottarakkara MC road, when he reached near Nellimoottil Pady junction, tipper lorry bearing registration no.KL-26-E-4943 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as 2025:KER:58900 a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The second respondent-owner remained ex- parte.
4. The first respondent-driver of the offending lorry filed written statement contending that the accident as narrated in the petition is false.

The averments in the petition regarding age, disability,
nature of injuries, period of treatment, occupation and income were disputed.
The compensation claimed was contended to be exorbitant.
5. The third respondent-insurer filed written statement admitting the policy.
The averments in the petition regarding age, disability, nature of injuries, period of treatment, occupation and income were disputed.
The compensation claimed was contended to be exorbitant.
6. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A16 series
were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the respondents.

7. The Tribunal on consideration of the 2025:KER:58900 documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the first respondent-driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 3,98,960/- together with interest @ 9%
per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the third respondent/insurer has come up in appeal.
8. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

sentences.text: 9. Heard both sides.
10. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following head is challenged by the third respondent- Compensation for permanent disability

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that when the disability was only 10% and in the absence of any evidence of loss of earning power, the Tribunal erred in granting an amount of 2,30,400/- as compensation for permanent disability.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned 2025:KER:58900 counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a Civil Police Officer in the Police Department sustained injuries in the accident resulting in the disability of 10% stated in Ext.A13, which has certainly affected his earning power and hence the Tribunal was justified in granting him compensation under this head.
10.1.
Here the fact that the claim petitioner at the time of the accident was working as a Civil Police Officer is not in dispute.
The claim petitioner does not have a case that he was unable to continue in service after the accident.
There is no evidence on record to show that there was any loss of income due to the accident.
Till his retirement at the age of 56 years, he would be getting salary, for which there is no loss.
Therefore, during the period of service, no amount is liable to be paid for loss of earning power.
However, after his retirement, the disability of 10% caused may affect his earning power.
The accident took place on 28/04/2015.
The claim petitioner was 31 years at the time of the accident.

The claim petitioner will superannuate at the age of 56 and therefore, when loss of earning power is considered for a period after retirement, the multiplier is to be applied is 9.
2025:KER:58900 11.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that in the light of the dictum in N.
Jayasree v. Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company, 2021 (6) KHC 163, split multiplier cannot be applied.

sentences.text: In the case on hand, no split multiplier is being applied.
The claim petitioner in the absence of any evidence of loss of earning power during the period of his service, is not entitled to any amount as compensation for the said period.
However, for the period after his retirement, he would be entitled for compensation for loss of earning power.
The notional income has been fixed as 12,000/- by the Tribunal.

Therefore, the amount to which he would be entitled will be 1,29,600/-,
that is, 12,000/- x 12 x 9 x 10/100.
12.
